verdict.rationale: Devin documents its own trigger-driven autonomy: Auto-Fix automatically responds to review comments and CI failures without a human in the loop, and it can be wired into CI/CD to act on static-analysis findings. Recurring schedules appear only as a single passing mention of 'scheduling' in the MCP server description, with no dedicated docs on configuring them. missing for 10: documented recurring schedule configuration, an explicit always-on/standing-agent setup beyond PR-scoped triggers, broader trigger types (e.g. monitoring or issue events), and independent hands-on corroboration of unattended scheduled runs.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: With Auto-Fix enabled, Devin automatically responds to code review comments, fixes flagged bugs, and iterates on CI failures — creating a closed loop where PRs iterate toward merge-ready quality without you in the loop.
Integrate Devin into your CI/CD pipeline to respond to findings from static analysis tools like SonarQube, Fortify, or Veracode.
it gives any MCP-compatible AI agent or IDE full access to session management, playbooks, knowledge, and scheduling
The cloud session gets its own VM with a shell, browser, and full repo access, so it can keep going after you close your laptop.
